parts.question: Compare AE evidence in HN-204 and HN-311.

result.answer: In HN-204, AX-17 treatment percentages for adverse events are 12.7% for nausea [E1, E3], 14.0% for headache [E1, E3], 15.3% for fatigue [E1, E3], 16.6% for dizziness [E1, E3], 17.8% for rash [E1, E3], and 19.1% for transaminase elevation [E1, E3]. Transaminase elevation is serious [E1]. In HN-311, AX-17 treatment percentages are 11.8% for nausea [E2, E3], 13.0% for headache [E2, E3], 14.2% for fatigue [E2, E3], 15.4% for dizziness [E2, E3], 16.6% for rash [E2, E3], and 17.7% for transaminase elevation [E2, E3]. Transaminase elevation is serious [E2]. Control percentages for all adverse events are identical in both studies at 6.0% for nausea [E1, E2, E3], 6.6% for headache [E1, E2, E3], 7.2% for fatigue [E1, E2, E3], 7.8% for dizziness [E1, E2, E3], 8.4% for rash [E1, E2, E3], and 9.0% for transaminase elevation [E1, E2, E3]. Comparing treatment percentages (HN-311 minus HN-204), differences are -0.9 points for nausea [E4], -1.0 points for headache [E4], -1.1 points for fatigue [E4], -1.2 points for dizziness [E4], -1.2 points for rash [E4], and -1.4 points for transaminase elevation [E4]. Control percentage difference is +0.0 points [E4].
